title: Synthesis and characterization of polynuclear lanthanide aryloxides

synthesis.procedure: Under N2 using glove-box and Schlenk techniques, europium metal was added to a solution of 1-naphthol in THF in a 250 ml Schlenk flask. The flask was connected to a vacuum line and liquid ammonia was condensed into the reaction vessel at −78 °C. After 3 h the mixture was allowed to warm slowly to room temperature and purged with N2, then filtered through Celite and evaporated. The product was washed several times with pentane and dried under vacuum to give an orange solid formulated as Eu4(OC10H7)8(THF)10. X-ray quality crystals of 1 were grown from a THF solution of the orange solid at room temperature.
synthesis.temperature: ammonia condensation at −78 °C, then warm to room temperature; crystallization at room temperature
synthesis.vessel_or_method: 250 ml Schlenk flask; liquid-ammonia metal-dissolution route under N2; vacuum-line condensation of NH3; Celite filtration
synthesis.workup_and_crystallization: filter through Celite, evaporate, wash with pentane, dry under vacuum; recrystallize from THF at room temperature

source_locations.location: Results and discussion; tetrameric Eu structure

synthesis.procedure: Ytterbium metal was added to a solution of 1-naphthol in THF and treated analogously to the europium reaction (liquid ammonia condensed at −78 °C, 3 h, warm to room temperature, N2 purge, Celite filtration, evaporation). A yellow solid formulated as Yb2(OC10H7)6(THF)4 was obtained. X-ray quality crystals of 2 were grown from a MeCN solution of the yellow solid at −20 °C.
synthesis.temperature: procedure as for 1 (NH3 at −78 °C then room temperature); crystallization at −20 °C
synthesis.time: similar to 1 (3 h at −78 °C before warming)
synthesis.vessel_or_method: Schlenk / liquid-ammonia metal-dissolution route as for 1
synthesis.workup_and_crystallization: same work-up as 1 to a yellow solid; crystals grown from MeCN at −20 °C

source_locations.location: Results and discussion; dimeric Yb structure, Fig. 2, Table 3
